anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly: The optimizer reuses or chooses a substantially sub-optimal execution plan despite correct statistics, leading to inefficient access paths, inappropriate join methods, or unstable plan flips.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly: Physical corruption or logical inconsistency inside data pages or index structures causes missing/duplicate rows, checksum failures, or unexpected engine errors, making the storage layer untrustworthy.

When both root causes are present, the database may exhibit extreme and erratic behaviour: the optimizer may alternate between inefficient full-table scans and corrupt-index-driven lookups, producing wildly varying runtimes, sporadic spikes in I/O and CPU, and unpredictable result sets that sometimes show missing or duplicated rows. Execution plans that appear reasonable in the cache can still fail at runtime with corruption or latch time-outs, while integrity-check errors surface intermittently. Sudden plan recompilations triggered by corruption-induced statistics divergence or failed index seeks can cause flurries of ad-hoc plans, exhausting cache memory and further destabilizing performance. Troubleshooting becomes difficult because poor performance, wrong results, and physical corruption errors mingle, obscuring which symptom stems from which layer.

Causally, damaged index or data pages distort cardinality feedback and may force the optimizer to rethink or invalidate previously good plans, increasing the likelihood of sub-optimal plan selection. Conversely, an already poor plan that overuses a corrupt index amplifies read amplification and exposes the corruption more frequently, accelerating error propagation and potential crash recovery events. The feedback loop between unreliable storage structures and volatile plan choices can therefore reinforce each anomaly, degrading throughput and reliability across both OLTP and analytic workloads.

entry.error_class: Class 42 - Syntax Error or Access Rule Violation
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with unsupported syntax, invalid statement structure, or feature usage that the target engine version cannot execute as written.
entry.solution_guidance: Validate SQL syntax, target-engine compatibility, statement shape, and whether the feature is supported under the current engine version or execution context.
